summary: The exact candidate is a substantive source implementation of the proposed RVV kernels, dispatch integration, tests, packaging, Dockerfile, and documentation. The recorded base concretely lacks the rvv CLI choice and RVV Python modules; the candidate makes those portable paths available and its non-native tests pass. However, the review host is x86_64, the imported native sgl_kernel remains the pre-existing x86_64 wheel, and no usable RISC-V sysroot/toolchain or RVV device is present. All 49 native numerical tests skip, a native rebuild cannot be completed, and the required Qwen2.5 GSM8K and RVV performance deliverables cannot run. Therefore the original target-hardware contract is not independently verified and cannot be marked fully resolved.

tests.command: base: python -m sglang.launch_server --help; import sglang.srt.layers.attention.rvv_backend and sglang.srt.layers.rvv_utils
tests.what_was_measured: On exact base 358c1632, the attention-backend choices do not contain rvv and both RVV module imports fail with ModuleNotFoundError, reproducing the feature absence. See base-feature-absence.log and base-import.log.

At exact candidate f8c062cb, 21 portable registration, dispatch, fallback, metadata, packing-cache, and server-argument tests passed; all 49 tests that require candidate native RVV operators skipped. See candidate-regression.log.

sglang and both new RVV Python modules imported from /job/repo, while sgl_kernel imported from /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sglang_kernel-0.4.6.post1-py3.12-linux-x86_64.egg. Thus Python tests used candidate source but no candidate native library. See candidate-import-paths.log.

tests.command: python -m compileall -q <new RVV Python modules>; independently parse --device cpu --attention-backend rvv; configure RVV CMake project
tests.what_was_measured: New Python modules compile, the CLI accepts the explicit rvv backend, and CMake configuration reaches generation. This is portable integration evidence only. See independent-adversarial.log.
The only pinned compiler accepts the RISC-V target flags but has no riscv_vector.h, so even header-level intrinsic validation is blocked. See native-compile-attempt.log.

A native build on x86_64 fails immediately because the RVV -mabi and -mrvv-vector-bits flags are unsupported for the host target. No candidate shared library was produced. See native-build-attempt.log.

gpu_execution.evidence: The feature targets RISC-V CPUs. GPU execution would not validate RVV, and no unrelated GPU smoke was substituted.

remaining_counterexamples: No candidate native operator executed: every activation, decode, extend, GEMM, INT8 GEMM, norm, and RoPE numerical case skipped on x86_64.
No RVV 1.0 instruction emission or disassembly was obtained from a rebuilt candidate library.
No end-to-end Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct GSM8K run was performed on a supported RISC-V/RVV system.
No RVV-versus-Torch-native performance comparison was performed on Banana Pi BPI-F3 or similar target hardware.
The linux/riscv64 Docker image and its vendor wheel availability were not independently built or validated.
remaining_limitations: Review machine: x86_64 AMD host, Linux 4.18; no RISC-V or RVV execution capability.
Pinned Torch is 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and its installed sgl_kernel is an x86_64 egg, not a candidate rebuild.
Pinned ROCm Clang 22 lacks riscv_vector.h; the environment has no RISC-V sysroot or target-native PyTorch libraries.
The tiny Llama serving fixture was not used because it cannot qualify RVV native correctness, Qwen architecture accuracy, or target-board performance.
